name: Flocculonodular lobe
summary: The oldest part of the cerebellum: the nodule of the vermis and the two flocculi that hang beneath the middle cerebellar peduncles at the cerebellopontine angles. It receives primary vestibular fibers directly from the vestibular nerve and secondary fibers from the vestibular nuclei, plus visual input from the accessory optic system, and projects back to the vestibular nuclei both directly and via the fastigial nucleus. It calibrates the vestibulo-ocular reflex, holds gaze eccentrically and stabilizes balance; lesions produce nystagmus and truncal imbalance without limb ataxia.

anatomy.location: Nodule in the midline in front of the uvula at the caudal end of the vermis, and the flocculus on each side in the cerebellopontine angle behind the cochlear nerve, connected to the nodule by a thin peduncle.

function: Vestibulo-ocular reflex gain adaptation, gaze holding, smooth pursuit, and vestibular control of posture and balance.

bestView.label: flocculus in the cerebellopontine angle behind the eighth nerve
nodule at the caudal vermis in front of the uvula

imaging.normalAppearance: The flocculus is a small lobulated structure in the cerebellopontine angle on axial T2 that can be mistaken for a mass; the nodule is seen at the caudal end of the vermis on sagittal images.

pathology.pathology: Flocculus mistaken for a CPA tumor
pathology.finding: Normal folia of the flocculus protruding into the cerebellopontine angle cistern; no enhancement, symmetric with the other side.
pathology.pitfalls: Compare with the opposite side before calling a cerebellopontine angle mass

pathology.finding: Small caudal vermian lesion with positional vertigo and downbeat nystagmus mimicking BPPV.

lesionEffects.deficit: Nystagmus: gaze-evoked, downbeat or periodic alternating
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of gaze holding and VOR calibration

examination: Eccentric gaze holding and nystagmus in all directions
Smooth pursuit of a slowly moving target
Romberg and gait; Dix–Hallpike showing atypical (downbeat, non-fatiguing) nystagmus
pearls: Downbeat nystagmus points to the craniocervical junction or the flocculus
Positional vertigo that does not fatigue and is downbeating is central until proven otherwise
